title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Roof soft washing
audience: Owners and crew leads in roof soft washing who quote roof cleaning, mould treatment and related add-ons, including solo operators.
learningOutcomes: Write a roof soft washing offer with a clear result, the roof areas named, conditions and a fix-first promise
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries, such as chemicals, runoff, mould return and height, and reduce them
Price roof packages on value, storey and access, then check them against your own hours

instruction.heading: What a roof customer buys
instruction.body: A roof customer buys a cleaned roof surface, with the roof areas named, a method they can read, and a clear line for any mould treatment. 'I will clean your roof' names a task. 'I will soft-wash the main roof and the garage roof, as measured at the site visit, with a written rinse and chemical plan, and I will not clean the gutters or the solar panels unless they are quoted separately' names the result and the limits. The limits protect the price.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up, and what the price evidence can bear
instruction.body: Use three tiers: a soft wash of a single-storey house; that wash plus a mould treatment; that treatment plus a mould inhibitor. Stepped packages are one way to present an offer (Jobber Academy, May 2021, updated 8 October 2024), though its examples are lawn care, house cleaning, car detailing and gutter cleaning, not roof cleaning. The price evidence is from What's The Damage, a lead-generation guide. It gives a soft wash for a single-storey house at $300 to $650, typical $480; a full-exterior mould treatment at $300 to $900, typical $550; and a mould inhibitor add-on at $50 to $150, typical $70. The same guide gives a mould treatment range of $300 to $1,300 in a later table, so the spread is unresolved. Its 'roof, standard home' band of $300 to $1,300, typical $900, does not say what work it covers, so do not use it as a soft-wash price. The guide gives no soft-wash figure for a double-storey house. Read all these as a reference band, not an average, and build your tiers from your own hours (see the roof BP-05 lesson).

instruction.heading: Quote from a site visit
instruction.body: The guide says quotes without a site visit are estimates. Record the roof's area and pitch at the site visit. This research found no per-square-metre or per-pitch price for roofs, so do not quote one. Show the storey and access as a line on the quote, with its reason. Gutter and downpipe work is a separate scope, not part of a soft wash (see the licence section below).

instruction.heading: Chemicals, claims and return of mould
instruction.body: Only supplier safety data sheets were found for sodium hypochlorite. They are not regulator guidance, so do not make chemical safety claims in the offer until you have read the product's data sheet and checked your state's rules. Do not promise that mould will not return: no source in this research gives a return interval. Do not state a result you have not seen. Offer a fix-first promise you can keep, because Consumer Victoria says a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge, though its page sets no fix window.

instruction.heading: One total, with GST stated
instruction.body: Show an all-in total for each tier and say whether GST is included. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (last modified 15 July 2026). Put the mould inhibitor and any gutter work on the quote as separate lines, not as a hidden extra at invoice.

instruction.heading: Height and licence scope, checked before the price
instruction.body: Roof work is work at height. The Commonwealth falls code (registered 2016) says roof edges need guard rails or equivalent edge protection, that fragile surfaces include cement sheeting, rusty metal, fibreglass and skylights, and that safety mesh stops internal falls but not edge falls. That code is not Victorian law. WorkSafe Victoria's August 2026 release says that allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Check the Victorian rule before any roof access, and do not quote a roof you cannot reach by a method you can justify. On licence scope, the Building and Plumbing Commission says cleaning is excluded from roofing (stormwater) work unless it connects, disconnects or alters the item, so a soft wash alone appears to fall outside the roofing licence. Confirm this before you quote any gutter or downpipe work.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a customer would repeat, naming the roof areas and the limits.
Inspect each roof area at the site visit, record area, pitch, storey and access, and note any fragile surface.
Build three tiers, price each from your own hours and the storey and access lines, then check the totals against the lead-generation band.
Write the chemical and rinse plan, and check the product's safety data sheet and your state's rules before you name any product.
Name the exclusions, including gutters, downpipes and solar panels unless they are separately quoted and their licence scope is checked.
Decide the fix-first window and check that you can keep it.
Show one all-in total for each tier and state whether GST is included.

workedExamples.situation: A single-storey house with a tile roof and a mould patch on the north side. The client wants the roof 'cleaned and made like new'. The owner has not been on the roof.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which tiers should the owner offer, and what should the quote say about the mould, the result and the access?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner offers the three tiers, with the mould treatment and the inhibitor as separate lines. The words 'made like new' are replaced with a result the owner can show, and the owner does not promise that mould will not return. Access is settled before the price: the owner checks the Victorian rule for roof work, and does not quote a method until that is done. As a reference only, the lead-generation typicals for a single-storey soft wash ($480) and a mould inhibitor ($70) add to $550. That is a sum of two typicals, not a quote for this roof. The owner's own hours decide the figure.

equipmentAndPpe: Package sheet with three tiers and the all-in total
Roof inspection record with area, pitch, storey, access and fragile surfaces
Chemical and rinse plan with the product's safety data sheet attached
Fall-prevention and access equipment as the Victorian working-at-height method requires; PPE as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}

commonErrors.error: Quoting a roof without inspecting it, so access and fragile surfaces are unknown
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect at the site visit, and record area, pitch, storey and access before pricing.

commonErrors.error: Using the roof band from the lead-generation guide as a soft-wash price
commonErrors.prevention: Use the soft-wash band only, and note that the roof band's scope is not stated.

commonErrors.error: Promising that mould will not return
commonErrors.prevention: State the result you can show, and the fix-first window you have set.

commonErrors.error: Including gutters or downpipes in a soft-wash package before the licence scope is checked
commonErrors.prevention: Quote gutters as a separate line only after the Victorian licence scope is confirmed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence. Victoria's roofing licence scope is set under the plumbing rules, and the Building and Plumbing Commission roofing page is listed in this lesson's sources. Confirm the scope before you quote gutter or downpipe work.

Working at height: the Commonwealth code (2015) and the NSW code (2019) are cited here and are not Victorian rules. Victoria was not checked for this draft. WorkSafe Victoria says allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Check the Victorian rule with WorkSafe Victoria before any roof access.

Chemicals and runoff: no regulator guidance on soft-wash chemicals was found, and the EPA Victoria car-repair sheet does not cover roof or building washing. Check the runoff rule with EPA Victoria and the product's safety data sheet before you name any chemical in a quote.
The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited, so the all-in total and GST status belong on every quote.

qualityStandard: Every roof quote names the areas, measured from the site visit, the storey, the access method, the exclusions and an all-in total with GST status.
Every chemical named in a quote has a checked safety data sheet and a recorded runoff method.
Every roof access is checked against the Victorian rule before the quote is sent.
documentationEvidence: Package sheet with the three tiers and the date it was set
Roof inspection record with area, pitch, storey, access and fragile surfaces
Chemical and rinse record with the safety data sheet and the date it was checked
summary: A roof customer buys named roof areas, a readable method and a fix-first promise.
Use lead-generation bands as a reference only, and inspect the roof before you price it.
Access, chemicals and gutter scope are visible lines, and each is checked against the Victorian rule before quoting.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an offer does the roof soft washing customer buy?
options: The named roof areas and a readable method, with the limits stated

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Taken from the SOL-03 research file (tactic 11); the page was not reopened for this variant. Misleading price statements are prohibited, and an all-in price with GST status is the safer presentation. Publisher: ACCC.

sourceReferences: What's The Damage, 'Pressure washing cost guide', https://whatsthedamage.com.au/pressure-washing-cost/, verified November 2026, metadata 2026-11-01. Lead-generation guide; roof and soft-wash bands are estimates; the mould treatment range is inconsistent within the page.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source. Supports: stepped packages.
INSEAD Knowledge, 'Small Change, Big Rewards', https://knowledge.insead.edu/marketing/small-change-big-rewards, 2 October 2025. Non-trade study.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault; no fix window given.

Building and Plumbing Commission (Victoria), 'Roofing (stormwater) work', https://www.bpc.vic.gov.au/plumbers/plumber-classes-and-categories/roofing-stormwater-work, last updated 30 June 2026. Supports: cleaning excluded from the scope unless the work connects, disconnects or alters the item; roof drainage and roof covering maintenance included, with exclusions.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law. Supports: roof edge protection, fragile surfaces, safety mesh limits.

SafeWork NSW, 'Managing the risk of falls at workplaces' code, https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0018/50076/Managing-the-risk-of-falls-at-workplaces-COP.pdf, cover dated August 2019. NSW only.

WorkSafe Victoria news release on falls risks in the solar sector, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-08/crackdown-falls-risks-solar-sector, 26 August 2026. Supports: allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful even with no incident. Aimed at solar; the principle is stated for any roof.

Note: no regulator guidance on soft-wash chemical use, storage, PPE or disposal was found; only supplier safety data sheets. Runoff rules for roof washing in Victoria are UNCONFIRMED. No roof-specific client, insurer or real-estate evidence was found.
